output.description: The output contract the run must satisfy (spec §22.7). EXTENDS the previously published shape rather than replacing it: `format` stays a STRING, because that is the type this schema has always declared and a client that sent {"format":"text"} keeps its exact meaning and its exact behaviour. What changes is that the value is now READ. Before 2026-08-01 every value of `format` was accepted and dropped, so `json_schema` here is a demand nothing could previously have relied on being ignored; an unrecognised value is now a 400 rather than a silent no-op, which is the one behaviour change and it converts a lie into a refusal. `additionalProperties` is false on THIS object only — a misspelled `schemas` must not be silently dropped, which is the whole defect being fixed — and the top-level body stays open (`delegations` and `delegation_budget` are load-bearing there and appear in no published schema).

format.description: `text` is the default and the pre-existing behaviour: free-form output, no validation. `json_schema` demands that the final output parse as JSON and validate against `schema`.

name.description: A name for the schema, forwarded to providers that require one (OpenAI's response_format.json_schema.name). Defaults to `output` when omitted.

schema.description: The JSON Schema 2020-12 document the output must satisfy. REQUIRED when format is json_schema. Per spec §22.7 it may not request executable code, remote references ($ref to another document), or unbounded recursive expansion.

strict.description: Whether the provider is asked to CONSTRAIN decoding to the schema rather than merely be instructed by it. Server-side validation runs either way: strict:false relaxes what the provider is asked to guarantee, never whether the answer is checked.
